root_cause.text: The async_hold queue was not being purged in all code paths that call tls_decrypt_async_wait(), causing skbs to leak when tls_strp_msg_hold() fails partway through and tls_decrypt_sg() falls back to synchronous mode without processing a complete record in fully-async mode.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold)` from a single call site in tls_sw_recvmsg() into tls_decrypt_async_wait() itself. The CVE description explicitly states: "This fixes a leak when tls_strp_msg_hold() fails part-way through, after having added some cloned skbs to the async_hold queue. tls_decrypt_sg() will then call tls_decrypt_async_wait() to process all pending decrypts, and drop back to synchronous mode, but tls_sw_recvmsg() only flushes the async_hold queue when one record has been processed in 'fully-async' mode, which may not be the case here." The patch centralizes the purge operation so that every caller of tls_decrypt_async_wait() (including the -EBUSY fallback path in tls_do_decryption()) automatically releases held skbs without relying on caller-specific cleanup logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Purge pending packets from async_hold queue when async decryption wait completes to prevent resource leaks.
intent_record.what: Added a call to `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold)` before the return statement in the `tls_decrypt_async_wait()` function, which clears all packets from the async_hold queue.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that any packets queued in the async_hold buffer are purged (freed) when the async decryption wait completes. Previously, these packets would remain in the queue, potentially causing a resource leak or stale packet references. Now they are explicitly cleaned up before returning the async wait error status.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant or incorrect async_hold queue purge that was causing premature skb cleanup after async decryption completion.
intent_record.what: Removed the `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold);` line that was called immediately after `tls_decrypt_async_wait(ctx);` in the tls_sw_recvmsg function.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the explicit purging of the async_hold queue after waiting for async decryption to complete. The queue will no longer be forcibly cleared at this point, potentially allowing queued skbs to persist or be handled differently by subsequent code paths.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by implementing the missing purge of the async_hold queue in the tls_decrypt_async_wait() code path. This prevents skb leaks that occur when async decryption falls back to synchronous mode without processing complete records, which is the exact scenario described in the vulnerability root cause.

The group removes a purge operation, but the vulnerability root cause is about async_hold queue NOT being purged in certain code paths. The group's intent (removing redundant purge) is opposite to what's needed to fix the vulnerability (ensuring purge happens in all necessary paths). This appears to be addressing a different issue or potentially exacerbating the original problem.

candidates.rationale: This return statement exits tls_decrypt_async_wait() without purging the async_hold queue. When tls_strp_msg_hold() fails partway through and the function returns early, any skbs already queued in async_hold are not processed, causing a resource leak. The function returns directly without ensuring the queue is drained in all code paths.

vuln_statements.explanation: This return statement at line 249 in tls_decrypt_async_wait() exits the function without purging the async_hold queue. When tls_strp_msg_hold() fails partway through and the function returns early with this statement, any skbs already queued in async_hold are not processed or drained, causing a resource leak. The vulnerable code path allows the function to return directly without ensuring all pending packets in the async_hold queue are purged in all code paths, which is the root cause of the skb leak when async decryption falls back to synchronous mode.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces two new helper functions `tls_decrypt_async_wait()` and `tls_encrypt_async_wait()` that factor out existing code patterns. The commit message explicitly states 'No functional changes' - it is purely a refactoring commit that extracts duplicated waiting logic into reusable functions. The new `tls_decrypt_async_wait()` function does not include any queue purging logic (the `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold)` call remains in the caller at line 2122). Since this is a refactoring commit with no functional changes, it neither introduces the bug nor fixes it. The vulnerable construct (missing async_hold queue purge in all code paths) is not present in this commit's changes - the purge call is still there in tls_sw_recvmsg(). The actual vulnerability would exist if the purge were missing from code paths that call tls_decrypt_async_wait(), but this commit doesn't change that.
